content.text:
I submitted **index 12 (Ni 0.61 / Sb 0.39)** as the best composition. It had the highest efficiency (EQE) of the three compositions I measured: **0.289%**. I used all 3 EQE measurements and all 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Ni fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 0.61 | 0.289 |
| 8 | 0.73 | 0.111 |
| 21 | 0.34 | 0.005 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is highest at compositions somewhat richer in Ni than Sb. It is near zero on the Sb-rich side and drops again at higher Ni. Three points can't pin the peak down, so a composition between index 8 and index 21 that I didn't measure (for example index 10, 11, 13 or 14) could beat index 12.
- **What XRD showed:** the NiSb₂O₆ crystal structure appears across the whole composition line. The Sb-rich end (index 28) also contains a separate Sb oxide. At the Ni-rich end (index 4), a weak peak that looks like NiO appears. Index 8 showed a single phase, but its EQE still dropped.
- **Why I chose index 8 for the last measurement:** it was the next single-phase composition toward the Ni-rich end. It turned out worse than index 12, so the peak isn't at the Ni-rich end, but I had no measurements left to test compositions on the Sb-rich side of index 12.
